hero: In a procedure room of a Quezon City tertiary hospital, a Filipino nephrology fellow holds an ultrasound probe over the left flank of a young Filipino woman lying prone, an attending nephrologist beside him watching the screen, a nurse recording blood pressure; clean bright clinical light, focused calm mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Each renal POCUS view answers one focused question and has a specific limitation.
figures.content: Five horizontal panels with simple probe-position icons and schematic images. 1 'Kidney: obstruction?' - dilated calyces graded mild to severe; limit 'early obstruction may not dilate; full bladder dilates both sides'. 2 'Kidney size and cortex: chronic?' - small bright kidney; limit 'diabetes and amyloidosis keep kidneys large'. 3 'Bladder: full or clotted?' - volume, catheter balloon; limit 'ascites mimics'. 4 'Lung and IVC: congested?' - B-lines, plethoric IVC; limit 'pneumonia, fibrosis; breathing and ventilation change IVC'. 5 'VExUS: venous congestion harming the kidney?' - hepatic, portal, intrarenal Doppler plus IVC 2 cm or more; limit 'needs Doppler skill; validated mostly after cardiac surgery (HR 3.69 for AKI)'. Footer: 'LUST: congestion relieved 78% vs 56%; no difference in death, MI or heart failure (HR 0.88)'.

figures.teaches: The preferred order of temporary dialysis catheter sites follows venous anatomy and long-term access preservation.
figures.content: Front-view torso outline with veins drawn: right internal jugular (green, '1st: straight path to SVC and right atrium'), femoral vein (green-yellow, '2nd: no pneumothorax; infection risk rises with body mass'), left internal jugular (amber, '3rd: tortuous path, poorer flow'), subclavian (red, 'Last: pneumothorax, stenosis can ruin future arm fistula'). Inset: ultrasound transverse neck view with jugular vein beside carotid artery and needle tip entering the vein. Footer: 'KDIGO 2012: site order Not Graded; ultrasound 1A; chest radiograph before first use of jugular or subclavian 1B'.
